subject: FinLytics: Post-demo recap & next steps — model fit, evals, regression concerns

Subject: FinLytics: Post-demo recap & next steps — model fit, evals, regression concerns

Hi Samantha and Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time to demo your ingestion pipeline and sample intents yesterday — really helpful context. Quick recap + recommended next steps so we can align on a pilot: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary intents: financial summarization, anomaly explanation, and regulatory Q&A.
- Latency target: P95 < 400ms for 512-token responses.
- Cost sensitivity: want to optimize for steady-state throughput during end-of-day batch jobs.
- Biggest risk: quality regression when model architecture/weights are updated — you mentioned a prior regression with another provider.

Model fit & recommended evals
- Baseline models to try in pilot: 
  - rwd-open-13B-q4 (good balance of quality vs cost; recommended starting point)
  - rwd-rlhf-7B (lower-cost alternative for high-volume workflows)
- Eval suite (we'll run these against your prompt set): relevance (R-1/R-2), hallucination rate (fact-checking against your ledger samples), guardrail trigger rate, and token-level latency.

Quality/regression controls we recommend
- Pin model versions for production routes (we use immutable model_version tags, e.g. rwd-open-13B-q4@20260220).
- Canary deploys: 5–20% traffic to new model + automated diff/regression checks vs baseline prompt set.
- Regression alerting: Redwood Optimize can trigger a regression alert when key metrics degrade beyond thresholds you set.

Attachments: I attached a short benchmark PDF and the prompt set we proposed for evaluation.

Suggested next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Vivek (SE) and your engineering lead to review evals and integration details — 30 mins.
2) Provide a sample of 1,000 real prompts and 100 gold responses for scoring.
3) 2-week pilot: baseline run, canary rollout for any subsequent model updates, and a regression diff report at the end.

Are you available for the technical call early next week? I can loop in Monica from CS if we move to a pilot.

Thanks,
Marissa

2) For pinning versions: is that something we can control from our side (i.e., pin to a model_version and then only upgrade by request), or does Redwood auto-upgrade endpoints?

We'll prepare the 1,000 prompts but would like to understand the mechanics before committing to a pilot.

Subject: Re: FinLytics: Post-demo recap & next steps — model fit, evals, regression concerns

Hi Tom — great questions. TL;DR: you control the model_version pinned to a route, and we provide automated diff/regression reports as part of the pilot. Details below.

Model pinning & upgrade policy
- Routes are configured with a model_version tag (immutable). By default, hosted demo routes use a floating alias (e.g., rwd-open-13B-q4_latest) but production routes can be pinned to an explicit immutable version: rwd-open-13B-q4@20260220.
- Only your org (FinLytics) or an authorized Redwood admin can change the pinned version for that route. We do not auto-upgrade pinned routes.

Diff / regression reporting workflow
- During canary/upgrade, we run the incoming canary traffic against both candidate and baseline versions and capture: metric diffs (precision/recall/F1), hallucination delta (measured by our fact-checker against provided gold data), guardrail trigger delta, and latency token-diffs.
- We produce a machine-readable diff CSV + human-friendly PDF summary. Example artifact: regression-diff-20260228.csv (attached) and a 6-page analysis PDF.
- If any metric breaches your thresholds (configurable), we mark the rollout as failed and automatically route traffic back to the pinned baseline. We also provide a rollback playbook with artifacts and reproducible eval commands.

What we need from you
- Gold labels for a representative subset (we recommend 100–200 items across intents) to measure hallucination/precision precisely.
- Baseline traffic window to sample realistic prompts (30–90 minutes of peak traffic or 1,000 prompts as Marissa suggested).

Links / artifacts
- Baseline benchmark doc: https://drive.google.com/finlytics-benchmarks-20260228
- Internal benchmark ID: RB-2026-FL-07

Happy to run through the exact commands and show a live diff in the technical call. If you want, we can also enable auto-snapshots of KV cache state and tokenizer checks to surface subtle regression sources (tokenization shifts, round-off differences after quantization).

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Technical call: Mon, 2 Mar at 11:00am PT — 30 minutes (Vivek will demo the diff report).
3) Pilot window: 2-week run starting after data ingest and baseline run (target start Wed, 4 Mar).
4) Acceptance criteria: no more than 3% drop in precision across priority intents; hallucination rate < 4%; P95 latency < 400ms.

Pilot controls we will enable:
- Pin baseline model: rwd-open-13B-q4@20260220
- Canary to candidate: 10% traffic for 48 hours with automated diff generation
- Auto-rollback if any configured metric breaches threshold

I attached the benchmark PDF and the prompt-set. We'll also prepare the regression-diff CSV template you'll receive after a canary run.

Could you confirm Mon 2 Mar 11:00am PT works for you? Also let me know if your SSO or firewall requires additional setup — Monica will coordinate on provisioning.
